items.title: FDA rejects Capricor deramiocel application over HOPE-3 data-integrity concerns
items.summary: The FDA issued Capricor a Complete Response Letter for deramiocel in Duchenne muscular dystrophy, citing inadequate efficacy evidence and serious trial-data integrity problems. Capricor disputes that characterization and is reviewing options. Shares plunged in Friday after-hours indications, not a confirmed regular-session close. The setback sharply reduces near-term approval certainty.

observations.label: FDA decision November 20, 2026
observations.value: FDA issued Complete Response Letter for resubmitted deramiocel BLA; agency said HOPE-3 data cannot be relied upon for approval because of unauthorized statistical-analysis changes, blinding breaches and protocol violations

observations.label: Company response and financial position
observations.value: Capricor says its HOPE-2/HOPE-3 trials met primary endpoints and contests FDA position; reported about $198.5 million cash, equivalents, restricted cash and marketable securities at September 30, 2026

observations.label: November 20 after-hours price observation (not official close)
observations.value: Reuters at approximately 6:44 PM EST reported CAPR down about 72% in extended trading; price moved further later in the evening; no Saturday US regular-session quote

observations.label: Risks, invalidation and next indicators
observations.value: Potential need for new reliable clinical evidence, prolonged approval delay and cash burn; company call November 23 at 8:30 AM EST, FDA correspondence and next study/remediation plan; new convincing data or altered FDA determination would change assessment

items.key_finding: FDA-confirmed rejection creates a severe regulatory and financing shock for CAPR; large share decline is after-hours, not a confirmed closing figure.

sources.title: FDA November 20 official statement on deramiocel application

items.title: WSJ reports UAE oil tanker shuttle strategy sustaining Hormuz shipments
items.summary: The Wall Street Journal reports ADNOC is using nighttime tanker convoys and offshore cargo transfers to sustain crude exports through Hormuz despite security threats. Historical exports recovered materially earlier in 2026, but recent transit counts are falling. The specific shuttle operation is single-source reporting; its current throughput and ability to withstand new attacks remain uncertain.

observations.label: November 21 WSJ reporting, observed 1:26 PM EST
observations.value: ADNOC-owned and chartered tankers reportedly shuttle crude at night across Hormuz and transfer offshore; WSJ reports UAE-linked strait exports reached about 2.1 million bpd in June versus 11,300 bpd in March

observations.label: Independent earlier regional-flow data
observations.value: Reuters November 3 citing Vortexa and another tracking provider reported broader Gulf oil/product exports averaging 17.1 million bpd in October vs 18.9 million in September; metrics and origins differ from WSJ UAE-specific series

observations.label: Latest maritime risk distinction
observations.value: UKMTO recorded 263 transits November 12-18 vs 308 prior week; lower visible vessel numbers do not establish proportional declines in cargo barrels because of AIS-dark voyages, load factors and offshore transfers

observations.label: Risks, invalidation and next indicators
observations.value: WSJ-specific operational detail not independently confirmed; monitor ADNOC statements, Kpler/Vortexa crude cargo flows, ship-to-ship activity, tanker incidents, UKMTO/MARAD, insurance costs; inability to sustain shuttle flow or clear new export declines weakens resilience assessment

items.key_finding: Single-source operational reporting helps explain why tanker counts may understate oil shipped, while recent physical-flow risks are rising.

sources.title: Wall Street Journal November 21 UAE oil shuttle report
Reuters November 3 regional Gulf crude and products data

items.title: Two additional UKMTO tanker strike notices near Khasab, Oman
items.summary: UKMTO warning 215-26 reports a tanker hit on its stern north of Khasab at 05:00 UTC Saturday. A separate warning 216-26 describes an engine-room strike east of Khasab at 05:50 UTC. Whether these are separate vessels remains uncertain. Neither report establishes a sustained crude-export shutdown.

observations.label: Warning 215-26, November 21 05:00 UTC
observations.value: Outbound tanker hit on stern by unidentified projectile, 11 nautical miles north of Khasab; UKMTO says no casualties initially; environmental impact unconfirmed

observations.label: Warning 216-26, November 21 05:50 UTC
observations.value: Outbound tanker reportedly hit in engine room by unidentified projectile, 17 nautical miles east of Khasab; no casualties initially reported; environmental impact unconfirmed

observations.label: Independent corroboration and uncertainty
observations.value: UKMTO official warning 215 and Clearwater Dynamics report of UKMTO 216; no independent ship identification, damage confirmation, or proof these are two distinct vessels

observations.label: Next indicators and invalidation
observations.value: Vessel identities, UKMTO/MARAD follow-ups, AIS transits, insurance and freight rates, Kpler/Vortexa oil loadings; uninterrupted flows and no further attacks would weaken prolonged-disruption concern

items.key_finding: Two new official tanker strike reports elevate Hormuz shipping danger; vessel count and oil-cargo losses are not yet verified.

sources.title: Clearwater Dynamics report on UKMTO Warning 216-26

items.title: Hormuz weekly transits fall 14.6%; tanker counts and preliminary oil flows also weaken
items.summary: UKMTO counted 263 combined transits for November 12–18, down from 308 the previous week, with traffic still far below pre-conflict levels. The Financial Times separately reports fewer tanker passages and weaker preliminary oil flows. Vessel counts are not equivalent to oil barrels, and dark transits may lead to revisions.

observations.label: UKMTO November 20 weekly report
observations.value: Nov 12–18: 115 outbound and 148 inbound = 263 combined transits; prior week 139 outbound and 169 inbound = 308; down 45 or 14.6%

observations.label: Comparison to pre-conflict baseline
observations.value: UKMTO estimates overall traffic around 65% below pre-conflict; some US-facilitated movements cannot be fully independently verified

observations.label: Financial Times independent report November 21
observations.value: Oil-tanker transits 37 vs 52 the prior week; preliminary second-week-November oil flows nearly half first-week levels, subject to dark-transit revisions

observations.label: Next indicators and invalidation
observations.value: Cross-check later AIS/UKMTO, Kpler/Vortexa oil volume, export loading and freight insurance; restored traffic and oil barrels would weaken physical-flow-disruption concern

items.key_finding: Observed vessel traffic is falling amid attacks; oil-flow magnitude remains preliminary and subject to revision.

sources.title: Financial Times November 21 Hormuz oil shipping report

items.title: Reuters sources say SEC examining potential Nvidia accounting issues
items.summary: Reuters reported that SEC enforcement staff are scrutinizing possible Nvidia accounting matters, citing two people briefed on the inquiry. The SEC declined comment, and the practices under review are unspecified. Nvidia shares fell sharply Friday, but most of the slide preceded the report. An inquiry does not establish wrongdoing.

observations.label: November 20, approximately 2:38 PM EST, Reuters
observations.value: Two people briefed on matter told Reuters SEC enforcement staff are examining potential Nvidia accounting issues; SEC declined comment; Nvidia response not available at publication

observations.label: Friday intraday market reaction
observations.value: Investing.com reports NVDA roughly -10% intraday and about -7% before Reuters accounting focus disclosure; incremental effect cannot be precisely attributed

observations.label: Fundamental assessment and limitations
observations.value: Actual accounting subject, timing, possible financial restatement and enforcement outcome are unknown; no wrongdoing proven; underlying AI chip orders not assessed by investigation report

observations.label: Next indicators / invalidation
observations.value: Nvidia SEC filings, auditor statements, investigation resolution, customer demand and revisions; closure without findings would weaken regulatory risk

items.key_finding: Reported SEC accounting focus compounds Nvidia uncertainty without establishing accounting violations.
